blocks.text: AREAS RELATED TO CIRCLES 11

blocks.label: Section-title
blocks.text: 11.1 Areas of Sector and Segment of a Circle

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
You have already come across the terms $sector$ and
$segment$ of a circle in your earlier classes. Recall
that the portion (or part) of the circular region enclosed
by two radii and the corresponding arc is called a
$sector$ of the circle and the portion (or part) of the
circular region enclosed between a chord and the
corresponding arc is called a $segment$ of the circle.
Thus, in Fig. 11.1, shaded region OAPB is a $sector$
of the circle with centre O. $\angle$ AOB is called the
$angle$ of the sector. Note that in this figure, unshaded region OAQB is also a sector of
the circle. For obvious reasons, OAPB is called the $minor$ $sector$ and
OAQB is called the $major$ $sector$. You can also see that angle of the major sector is
$360^\circ - \angle$ AOB.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Now, look at Fig. 11.2 in which AB is a chord
of the circle with centre O. So, shaded region APB is
a segment of the circle. You can also note that
unshaded region AQB is another segment of the circle
formed by the chord AB. For obvious reasons, APB
is called the $minor$ $segment$ and AQB is called the
$major$ $segment$.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Remark : When we write ‘segment’ and ‘sector’
we will mean the ‘minor segment’ and the ‘minor
sector’ respectively, unless stated otherwise.

blocks.label: Chapter-title
blocks.text: AREAS RELATED TO CIRCLES

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Now with this knowledge, let us try to find some
relations (or formulae) to calculate their areas.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Let OAPB be a sector of a circle with centre
O and radius $r$ (see Fig. 11.3). Let the degree
measure of $\angle AOB$ be $\theta$.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
You know that area of a circle (in fact of a
circular region or disc) is $\pi r^2$.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
In a way, we can consider this circular region to
be a sector forming an angle of $360^{\circ}$ (i.e., of degree
measure 360) at the centre O. Now by applying the
Unitary Method, we can arrive at the area of the
sector OAPB as follows:

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
When degree measure of the angle at the centre is 360, area of the
sector $= \pi r^2$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
So, when the degree measure of the angle at the centre is 1, area of the
sector = $\frac{\pi r^2}{360}$.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Therefore, when the degree measure of the angle at the centre is $\theta$, area of the

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$ \text{sector} = \frac{\pi r^2}{360} \times \theta = \frac{\theta}{360} \times \pi r^2 . $$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Thus, we obtain the following relation (or formula) for area of a sector of a
circle:

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: Area of the sector of angle $\theta = \frac{\theta}{360} \times \pi r^2$,

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: where $r$ is the radius of the circle and $\theta$ the angle of the sector in degrees.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Now, a natural question arises : Can we find
the length of the arc APB corresponding to this
sector? Yes. Again, by applying the Unitary
Method and taking the whole length of the circle
(of angle $360^{\circ}$) as $2\pi r$, we can obtain the required
length of the arc APB as $\frac{\theta}{360} \times 2\pi r$.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: So, length of an arc of a sector of angle $\theta = \frac{\theta}{360} \times 2\pi r$.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Now let us take the case of the area of the
segment APB of a circle with centre O and radius $r$
(see Fig. 11.4). You can see that :

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
Area of the segment APB = Area of the sector OAPB – Area of $\Delta$ OAB
$$= \frac{\theta}{360} \times \pi r^2$ – area of $\Delta$ OAB

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: **Note :** From Fig. 11.3 and Fig. 11.4 respectively, you can observe that:

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Area of the major sector OAQB = $\pi r^2$ – Area of the minor sector OAPB
and      Area of major segment AQB = $\pi r^2$ – Area of the minor segment APB
Let us now take some examples to understand these concepts (or results).

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Let us now take some examples to understand these concepts (or results).

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
Example 1 : Find the area of the sector of a circle
with radius 4 cm and of angle $30^{\circ}$. Also, find the area
of the corresponding major sector (Use $\pi = 3.14$).

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Solution : Given sector is OAPB (see Fig. 11.5).

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
$$Area\ of\ the\ sector\ =\ \frac{\theta}{360}\times\pi r^2$$

$$=\ \frac{30}{360}\times3.14\times4\times4\ cm^2$$

$$=\ \frac{12.56}{3}\ cm^2=4.19cm^2\ (approx.)$$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
Area of the corresponding major sector
$$ = \pi r^2 - \text{area of sector OAPB} $$
$$ = (3.14 \times 16 - 4.19) \text{ cm}^2 $$
$$ = 46.05 \text{ cm}^2 = 46.1 \text{ cm}^2 (\text{approx.}) $$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
Alternatively, area of the major sector = $\frac{(360 - \theta)}{360} \times \pi r^2$

$$= \left( \frac{360 - 30}{360} \right) \times 3.14 \times 16 \text{ cm}^2$$

$$= \frac{330}{360} \times 3.14 \times 16 \text{cm}^2 = 46.05 \text{ cm}^2$$

$$= 46.1 \text{ cm}^2 \text{ (approx.)}$$

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
Example 2 : Find the area of the segment AYB
shown in Fig. 11.6, if radius of the circle is 21 cm and
$\angle \text{AOB} = 120^{\circ}$. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$ )

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
Solution : Area of the segment AYB
$$= \text{Area of sector OAYB} - \text{Area of } \Delta \text{ OAB} \quad (1)$$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: Now, area of the sector OAYB = $\frac{120}{360} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 21 \times 21 \text{ cm}^2 = 462 \text{ cm}^2$ (2)

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
For finding the area of $\Delta$ OAB, draw OM $\perp$ AB as shown in Fig. 11.7.

Note that OA = OB. Therefore, by RHS congruence, $\Delta$ AMO $\cong \Delta$ BMO.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: So, M is the mid-point of AB and $\angle \text{AOM} = \angle \text{BOM} = \frac{1}{2} \times 120^\circ = 60^\circ$.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: Let $OM = x \text{ cm}$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: So, from $\Delta$ OMA, $\frac{\text{OM}}{\text{OA}} = \cos 60^\circ$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: or, $$\frac{x}{21} = \frac{1}{2} \left( \cos 60^\circ = \frac{1}{2} \right)$$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: So, $OM = \frac{21}{2} \text{ cm}$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: Also, $\frac{\text{AM}}{\text{OA}} = \sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: So, $AM = \frac{21\sqrt{3}}{2}$ cm

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: Therefore, $AB = 2 AM = \frac{2 \times 21\sqrt{3}}{2} \text{ cm} = 21\sqrt{3} \text{ cm}$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
So, $\text{area of } \Delta \text{ OAB} = \frac{1}{2} \text{ AB} \times \text{ OM} = \frac{1}{2} \times 21\sqrt{3} \times \frac{21}{2} \text{ cm}^2$
$= \frac{441}{4} \sqrt{3} \text{ cm}^2$ (3)

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
Therefore, area of the segment AYB = $\left(462-\frac{441}{4}\sqrt{3}\right)\mathrm{cm}^2$ [From (1), (2) and (3)]

$$=\frac{21}{4}(88-21\sqrt{3})\mathrm{cm}^2$$

blocks.label: Section-title
blocks.text: EXERCISE 11.1

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Unless stated otherwise, use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$.

blocks.label: List
blocks.text:
1. Find the area of a sector of a circle with radius 6 cm if angle of the sector is $60^{\circ}$.
2. Find the area of a quadrant of a circle whose circumference is 22 cm.
3. The length of the minute hand of a clock is 14 cm. Find the area swept by the minute
hand in 5 minutes.
4. A chord of a circle of radius 10 cm subtends a right angle at the centre. Find the area of
the corresponding : (i) minor segment (ii) major sector. (Use $\pi = 3.14$)
5. In a circle of radius 21 cm, an arc subtends an angle of $60^{\circ}$ at the centre. Find:
(i) the length of the arc (ii) area of the sector formed by the arc
(iii) area of the segment formed by the corresponding chord
6. A chord of a circle of radius 15 cm subtends an angle of $60^{\circ}$ at the centre. Find
the areas of the corresponding minor and major
segments of the circle.
(Use $\pi = 3.14$ and $\sqrt{3} = 1.73$)
7. A chord of a circle of radius 12 cm subtends an
angle of $120^{\circ}$ at the centre. Find the area of the
corresponding segment of the circle.
(Use $\pi = 3.14$ and $\sqrt{3} = 1.73$)
8. A horse is tied to a peg at one corner of a square
shaped grass field of side 15 m by means of a 5 m
long rope (see Fig. 11.8). Find

blocks.label: List
blocks.text:
(i) the area of that part of the field in which the
horse can graze.

(ii) the increase in the grazing area if the rope
were 10 m long instead of 5 m. (Use $\pi = 3.14$)

blocks.label: Question
blocks.text:
9. A brooch is made with silver wire in the form
of a circle with diameter 35 mm. The wire is also
used in making 5 diameters which divide the
circle into 10 equal sectors as shown in
Fig. 11.9. Find:

blocks.label: List
blocks.text:
(i) the total length of the silver wire required.
(ii) the area of each sector of the brooch.

blocks.label: Question
blocks.text:
10. An umbrella has 8 ribs which are equally spaced
(see Fig. 11.10). Assuming umbrella to be a flat
circle of radius 45 cm, find the area between the
two consecutive ribs of the umbrella.

blocks.label: Question
blocks.text:
11. A car has two wipers which do not overlap. Each
wiper has a blade of length 25 cm sweeping
through an angle of $115^{\circ}$. Find the total area
cleaned at each sweep of the blades.

blocks.label: Question
blocks.text:
12. To warn ships for underwater rocks, a lighthouse
spreads a red coloured light over a sector of
angle $80^{\circ}$ to a distance of 16.5 km. Find the area
of the sea over which the ships are warned.
(Use $\pi = 3.14$)

blocks.label: Question
blocks.text:
13. A round table cover has six equal designs as
shown in Fig. 11.11. If the radius of the cover is
28 cm, find the cost of making the designs at the
rate of $₹$ 0.35 per $\text{cm}^2$. (Use $\sqrt{3} = 1.7$)

blocks.label: MCQ
blocks.text:
14. Tick the correct answer in the following :
Area of a sector of angle $p$ (in degrees) of a circle
with radius R is

(A) $\frac{p}{180} \times 2\pi\text{R}$      (B) $\frac{p}{180} \times \pi\text{R}^2$      (C) $\frac{p}{360} \times 2\pi\text{R}$      (D) $\frac{p}{720} \times 2\pi\text{R}^2$

blocks.label: Section-title
blocks.text: 11.2 Summary

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: In this chapter, you have studied the following points :

blocks.label: List
blocks.text:
1. Length of an arc of a sector of a circle with radius $r$ and angle with degree measure $\theta$ is
$$\frac{\theta}{360} \times 2\pi r.$$

2. Area of a sector of a circle with radius $r$ and angle with degree measure $\theta$ is $\frac{\theta}{360} \times \pi r^2.$

3. Area of segment of a circle
= Area of the corresponding sector – Area of the corresponding triangle.
